channel.title: ZeroErrorEnglish - English Grammar Blog & Exam Strategy
channel.description: High-yield English grammar rules, bracket-elimination strategies, and book previews for Indian competitive exams (SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC CDS/NDA, State PSC).

item.title: Gerund or Infinitive After Verb? The Complete List for Bank PO Exams
item.description: Eight out of ten Bank PO aspirants lose easy marks not because they don't know grammar — but because they guess between 'enjoy swimming' and 'enjoy to swim' by ear. Here is the complete, memorizable list that ends the guessing forever.

item.title: Sequence of Tenses Rules for Competitive Exams — Direct & Indirect Speech Explained
item.description: Why does 'He said he is tired' feel right but score zero in SSC CGL? The Sequence of Tenses rule silently governs every Direct-to-Indirect conversion — and most aspirants have never learned it as a standalone rule. Here is the complete backshift system explained.

item.title: Articles Before Vowel Sounds — Why 'An Hour' Is Correct But 'A Hour' Is Wrong
item.description: Still choosing 'a' or 'an' by looking at the first letter? That's the trap. The real rule is about sound, not spelling — and this one mistake costs students marks in Class 12 boards and every major competitive exam.

item.title: Conditional Sentences: How SSC & IBPS Trick You With 'Had + Would Have' Traps
item.description: Why do exam boards repeat the Third Conditional error every single year? Because students keep placing 'would have' inside the 'if-clause'. Here is the foolproof formula to lock in full marks.

item.title: Subject-Verb Agreement in Inverted Sentences: The 3-Second Bracket Rule That Never Fails
item.description: Ever stared at an error-spotting question starting with 'Hardly', 'Seldom', or 'Along the river bank', and wondered why your gut feeling failed you? Here is the bracket-elimination technique my classroom students have used for 22 years.
